notes.front: In the volunteer examiner programme, what is reimbursement?
notes.back: Repayment by examinees of VEs’ and VECs’ out-of-pocket expenses in preparing, processing, administering or coordinating an examination.
notes.explanation: The repayment covers out-of-pocket expenses only, and comes from the examinees.
notes.example: Like a club passing round a hat to cover the hall hire and photocopying, but with no profit.
notes.source: 47 CFR Part 97 (rev. 1 Oct 2025), § 97.527 Reimbursement for expenses
notes.evidence: VEs and VECs may be reimbursed by examinees for out-of-pocket expenses incurred in preparing, processing, administering, or coordinating an examination for an amateur operator license.

notes.front: What is a question pool?
notes.back: All current examination questions for a designated written examination element.
notes.explanation: A question set for one examination is then selected from that pool.
notes.example: Like a published bank of driving-theory questions from which each candidate’s test is drawn.
notes.evidence: Question pool. All current examination questions for a designated written examination element. (36) Question set. A series of examination questions on a given examination selected from the question pool.

notes.front: What is Element 4?
notes.back: The written examination for the Amateur Extra Class licence: 50 questions, with 37 correct needed to pass.
notes.explanation: Its questions concern the privileges of an Amateur Extra Class operator licence.
notes.example: Like the final paper of a three-part qualification, longer than the two before it.
notes.evidence: Element 4: 50 questions concerning the privileges of an Amateur Extra Class operator license. The minimum passing score is 37 questions answered correctly.

notes.front: For an external RF power amplifier, what is certification?
notes.back: An FCC grant, under subpart J of Part 2, that an amplifier made or imported for amateur use must have.
notes.explanation: No amplifier able to operate below 144 MHz may be built or modified by a non-amateur without such a grant.
notes.example: Like a type-approval stamp a car model needs before it can be sold.
notes.source: 47 CFR Part 97 (rev. 1 Oct 2025), § 97.315(a) Certification of external RF power amplifiers
notes.evidence: manufactured or imported for use at an amateur radio station must be certificated for use in the amateur service in accordance with subpart J of part 2 of the FCC Rules. No amplifier capable of operation below 144 MHz may be constructed or modified by a non-amateur service licensee without a grant of certification from the FCC.

notes.front: What is Line A?
notes.back: A line defined in Part 97 that runs from Aberdeen, Washington, eastward to Searsport, Maine.
notes.explanation: Its course runs by great circle arcs and along the 48° N parallel, among other lines.
notes.example: Like a boundary drawn a little inside a national border, marking where a rule starts to apply.
notes.evidence: Line A. Begins at Aberdeen, WA, running by great circle arc to the intersection of 48° N, 120° W, thence along parallel 48° N, to the intersection of 95° W,

notes.front: What is a Special Temporary Authority (STA)?
notes.back: A temporary authority the FCC may issue to an amateur station, for instance to provide for experimental amateur communications.
notes.explanation: The pool gives experimental communications as the circumstance, not special event call signs or exam sessions.
notes.example: Like a short-term permit for a one-off trial that the ordinary rules do not cover.
notes.evidence: Under what circumstances might the FCC issue a Special Temporary Authority (STA) to an amateur station? A. To provide for experimental amateur communications

notes.front: In Part 97, what is barred by the rule on pecuniary interest?
notes.back: Communications in which the licensee or control operator has a pecuniary interest, including those on behalf of an employer.
notes.explanation: The rule then lists a few exceptions.
notes.example: Like a volunteer marshal who may help at a race but may not advertise the family shop over the tannoy.
notes.evidence: Communications in which the station licensee or control operator has a pecuniary interest, including communications on behalf of an employer, with the following exceptions:

notes.front: Each question pool must contain at least {{c1::10 times}} the number of questions required for a single examination.
notes.back: 10 times
notes.explanation: Section 97.523 also has all VECs cooperate in keeping one pool for each written element.
notes.evidence: All VECs must cooperate in maintaining one question pool for each written examination element. Each question pool must contain at least 10 times the number of questions required for a single examination.

notes.front: When must a question pool be made public?
notes.back: Before it is used to make a question set.
notes.explanation: Each question must also be prepared by a VE holding the required FCC licence.
notes.evidence: Each question pool must be published and made available to the public prior to its use for making a question set. Each question on each VEC question pool must be prepared by a VE holding the required FCC-issued operator license.

notes.front: What must an organisation have with the FCC before it may serve as a VEC?
notes.back: A written agreement with the FCC, whose terms it must then follow.
notes.explanation: Section 97.521 makes the agreement the gateway to serving as a VEC.
notes.evidence: No organization may serve as a VEC unless it has entered into a written agreement with the FCC. The VEC must abide by the terms of the agreement.

notes.front: What are two conditions an organisation must meet to be eligible as a VEC?
notes.back: Any two of: it exists to further the amateur service; it coordinates exams for any licence class; it registers every qualified examinee without discrimination.
notes.explanation: Registration must be without regard to race, sex, religion, national origin or organisation membership.
notes.evidence: (c) Agree to coordinate examinations for any class of amateur operator license; (d) Agree to assure that, for any examination, every examinee qualified under these rules is registered without regard to race, sex, religion, national origin or membership (or lack thereof) in any amateur service organization;

notes.front: Since 10 February 2026, must a VEC be able to serve a particular VEC region?
notes.back: No: the FCC removed 97.521(b) and the VEC regions of Appendix 2.
notes.explanation: The FCC called the region-based test unnecessary because VECs now allow and offer remote exams.
notes.source: Federal Register 2025-22633 (12 Dec 2025), direct final rule, ¶ on obsolete rules
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · Part 97 as amended by FR 2025-22633, effective 10 Feb 2026
notes.evidence: Sec. 97.521(b) (providing volunteer-examiner coordinator (VEC) qualifications provision based on serving in specific regions, which are unnecessary because remote exams are now allowed and offered by VEC organizations);

notes.front: What are two grounds on which a VEC must not accredit a person as a VE?
notes.back: Any two of: fails minimum qualifications; FCC won’t accept their voluntary, uncompensated service; not competent; integrity or honesty questions.
notes.explanation: Most grounds are determinations by the VEC; one is the FCC declining the person’s services.
notes.evidence: (2) The FCC does not accept the voluntary and uncompensated services of the person; (3) The VEC determines that the person is not competent to perform the VE functions; or (4) The VEC determines that questions of the person's integrity or honesty could compromise the examinations.

notes.front: How old must an administering VE be?
notes.back: At least 18.
notes.explanation: Each administering VE must also be accredited by the coordinating VEC.
notes.source: 47 CFR Part 97 (rev. 1 Oct 2025), § 97.509(b) Administering VE requirements
notes.evidence: Each administering VE must: (1) Be accredited by the coordinating VEC; (2) Be at least 18 years of age;

notes.front: Whose licence history bars them from being an administering VE?
notes.back: Anyone whose amateur station or operator licence grant has ever been revoked or suspended.
notes.explanation: The rule says “ever”, so a past revocation or suspension counts.
notes.source: 47 CFR Part 97 (rev. 1 Oct 2025), § 97.509(b)(4) Administering VE requirements
notes.evidence: Not be a person whose grant of an amateur station license or amateur operator license has ever been revoked or suspended.

notes.front: How many VEs must administer each amateur licence examination?
notes.back: A team of at least 3, at a session coordinated by a VEC.
notes.explanation: The number of examinees at the session may be limited.
notes.source: 47 CFR Part 97 (rev. 1 Oct 2025), § 97.509(a) Administering VE requirements
notes.evidence: Each examination for an amateur operator license must be administered by a team of at least 3 VEs at an examination session coordinated by a VEC. The number of examinees at the session may be limited.

notes.front: Each administering VE must observe the examinee throughout the {{c1::entire examination}}.
notes.back: entire examination
notes.explanation: The administering VEs are responsible for the proper conduct and necessary supervision of each examination.
notes.source: 47 CFR Part 97 (rev. 1 Oct 2025), § 97.509(c) Administering VE requirements
notes.evidence: Each administering VE must observe the examinee throughout the entire examination. The administering VEs are responsible for the proper conduct and necessary supervision of each examination.

notes.front: No VE may examine a spouse, children, grandchildren, stepchildren, parents, grandparents, stepparents, siblings, step-siblings, aunts, uncles, nieces, nephews or {{c1::in-laws}}.
notes.back: in-laws
notes.explanation: Section 97.509(d) names these relatives; the list ends with in-laws.
notes.source: 47 CFR Part 97 (rev. 1 Oct 2025), § 97.509(d) Administering VE requirements
notes.evidence: No VE may administer an examination to his or her spouse, children, grandchildren, stepchildren, parents, grandparents, stepparents, brothers, sisters, stepbrothers, stepsisters, aunts, uncles, nieces, nephews, and in-laws.

notes.front: When must the administering VEs grade an examinee’s answers?
notes.back: Immediately after each element; for remote exams, at the earliest practical opportunity.
notes.explanation: The administering VEs are responsible for deciding whether answers are correct.
notes.source: 47 CFR Part 97 (rev. 1 Oct 2025), § 97.509(h) Administering VE requirements
notes.evidence: Upon completion of each examination element, the administering VEs must immediately grade the examinee's answers. For examinations administered remotely, the administering VEs must grade the examinee's answers at the earliest practical opportunity.

notes.front: Certifying VEs may hand other qualified VEs the job of giving individual elements. What may they not hand over?
notes.back: Their accountability; they may delegate only their authority.
notes.explanation: The certifying VEs are jointly and individually accountable for each element reported.
notes.source: 47 CFR Part 97 (rev. 1 Oct 2025), § 97.509(i) Administering VE requirements
notes.evidence: The certifying VEs are jointly and individually accountable for the proper administration of each examination element reported. The certifying VEs may delegate to other qualified VEs their authority, but not their accountability, to administer individual elements of an examination.

notes.front: What must the administering VEs issue to an examinee who passes an examination element?
notes.back: A CSCE.
notes.explanation: Section 97.509(l) ties the certificate to each element passed.
notes.source: 47 CFR Part 97 (rev. 1 Oct 2025), § 97.509(l) Administering VE requirements
notes.evidence: The administering VEs must issue a CSCE to an examinee who scores a passing grade on an examination element.

notes.front: Which is the lowest-frequency segment where 97.305(c) authorises SS emissions?
notes.back: 222–225 MHz, in the 1.25 m band.
notes.explanation: The 219–220 MHz segment just below it is authorised for data only.
notes.source: 47 CFR Part 97 (rev. 1 Oct 2025), § 97.305(c) Authorized emission types (table)
notes.evidence: (iv) 1.25 m | 219-220 MHz | Data | (f)(13). | (v) 1.25m | 222-225 MHz | RTTY, data, test MCW, phone, SS, image

notes.front: May SS emissions be used to hide the meaning of a communication?
notes.back: No: 97.311(a) says SS must not be used to obscure the meaning of any communication.
notes.explanation: The rule covers any communication sent by SS.
notes.source: 47 CFR Part 97 (rev. 1 Oct 2025), § 97.311(a) SS emission types
notes.evidence: SS emission transmissions must not be used for the purpose of obscuring the meaning of any communication.

notes.front: Who may not build or modify an amplifier able to operate below 144 MHz without a grant of certification?
notes.back: A non-amateur service licensee.
notes.explanation: The rule covers amplifiers capable of operation below 144 MHz.
notes.source: 47 CFR Part 97 (rev. 1 Oct 2025), § 97.315(a) Certification of external RF power amplifiers
notes.evidence: No amplifier capable of operation below 144 MHz may be constructed or modified by a non-amateur service licensee without a grant of certification from the FCC.

notes.front: What did the FCC do with 97.315(b)(2), the pre-1978 amplifier exception, from 10 February 2026?
notes.back: Removed it and reserved the paragraph.
notes.explanation: The FCC judged a provision about equipment almost 50 years old no longer necessary.
notes.source: Federal Register 2025-22633 (12 Dec 2025), direct final rule, ¶ on obsolete rules
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · Part 97 as amended by FR 2025-22633, effective 10 Feb 2026
notes.evidence: Sec. 97.315(b)(2) (discussing certification of external RF power amplifiers for equipment that is almost 50 years old, making the provision no longer necessary);

notes.front: To be certificated, an amplifier must not amplify its driving signal by more than {{c1::15 dB}}.
notes.back: 15 dB
notes.explanation: Gain is the ratio of input to output power, both measured as peak envelope power or mean power.
notes.source: 47 CFR Part 97 (rev. 1 Oct 2025), § 97.317(a)(2) Standards for certification of external RF power amplifiers
notes.evidence: Not be capable of amplifying the input RF power (driving signal) by more than 15 dB gain. Gain is defined as the ratio of the input RF power to the output RF power of the amplifier where both power measurements are expressed in peak envelope power or mean power.

notes.front: How much gain may a certificated amplifier have between 26 MHz and 28 MHz?
notes.back: None: 0 dB.
notes.explanation: Certification is also denied if the amplifier can be easily modified to work there.
notes.source: 47 CFR Part 97 (rev. 1 Oct 2025), § 97.317 Standards for certification of external RF power amplifiers
notes.evidence: Exhibit no amplification (0 dB gain) between 26 MHz and 28 MHz. (b) Certification shall be denied when: (1) The Commission determines the amplifier can be used in services other than the Amateur Radio Service, or (2) The amplifier can be easily modified to operate on frequencies between 26 MHz and 28 MHz.

notes.front: Where does Line A end?
notes.back: At the southernmost point of Searsport, Maine.
notes.explanation: Its last legs run through the southernmost points of Bangor and then Searsport.
notes.evidence: thence by great circle arc through the southernmost point of Bangor, ME, thence by great circle arc through the southernmost point of Searsport, ME, at which point it terminates.

notes.front: When may a control operator accept pay connected with using an amateur station?
notes.back: Among other exceptions, as part of a teaching position, while the station is used in classroom instruction at an educational institution.
notes.explanation: It applies only while the station is used as part of classroom instruction.
notes.evidence: A control operator may accept compensation as an incident of a teaching position during periods of time when an amateur station is used by that teacher as a part of classroom instruction at an educational institution.

notes.front: May an amateur tell others on the air that station equipment is for sale?
notes.back: Yes, for apparatus normally used in an amateur station, provided it is not done on a regular basis.
notes.explanation: The activity must not be conducted on a regular basis.
notes.evidence: An amateur operator may notify other amateur operators of the availability for sale or trade of apparatus normally used in an amateur station, provided that such activity is not conducted on a regular basis.

notes.front: On which bands may an auxiliary station transmit?
notes.back: The 2 m and shorter-wavelength bands, apart from certain listed segments.
notes.explanation: The excluded segments include 144.0–144.5 MHz and 435–438 MHz, among others.
notes.evidence: An auxiliary station may transmit only on the 2 m and shorter wavelength bands, except the 144.0-144.5 MHz, 145.8-146.0 MHz, 219-220 MHz, 222.00-222.15 MHz, 431-433 MHz, and 435-438 MHz segments.

notes.front: A VE on the team sees that her stepbrother has registered to sit Element 3. What must she do?
notes.choices:
A) Administer it, since step-relatives are not blood relatives
B) Administer it if two other VEs also grade it
C) Not administer his examination
D) Administer it only if the VEC agrees in writing
notes.back: Not administer his examination
notes.choicesExplained: A: the list names step-relatives expressly. B and D: the rule has no such exceptions.
notes.explanation: Stepbrothers are on the 97.509(d) list of relatives a VE may not examine.
notes.source: 47 CFR Part 97 (rev. 1 Oct 2025), § 97.509(d) Administering VE requirements
notes.evidence: No VE may administer an examination to his or her spouse, children, grandchildren, stepchildren, parents, grandparents, stepparents, brothers, sisters, stepbrothers, stepsisters, aunts, uncles, nieces, nephews, and in-laws.

notes.front: An examinee has just passed the last element needed for a new licence. What are two things the VE team must then do?
notes.back: Any two of: issue a CSCE; have three VEs certify the examinee is qualified; submit the application document to the coordinating VEC.
notes.explanation: Section 97.509(m) sets the last step: the application document goes to the coordinating VEC.
notes.source: 47 CFR Part 97 (rev. 1 Oct 2025), § 97.509(m) Administering VE requirements
notes.evidence: After the administration of a successful examination for an amateur operator license, the administering VEs must submit the application document to the coordinating VEC according to the coordinating VEC's instructions.

notes.front: An Element 4 examination has 50 questions. What is the smallest Element 4 question pool that 97.523 allows?
notes.back: 500 questions.
notes.explanation: A pool must hold at least 10 times the questions needed for a single examination, and 10 × 50 = 500.
notes.evidence: Each question pool must contain at least 10 times the number of questions required for a single examination.

notes.front: A maker designs an HF external amplifier with 20 dB of gain, clean spurious emissions and no gain from 26 to 28 MHz. Can it be certificated?
notes.choices:
A) Yes, because its spurious emissions meet the standard
B) Yes, if it is sold only to amateurs
C) No: its gain exceeds 15 dB
D) No: HF amplifiers cannot be certificated
notes.back: No: its gain exceeds 15 dB
notes.choicesExplained: A: meeting one standard does not excuse failing another. B: selling only to amateurs does not change the certification standards. D: HF amplifiers can be certificated if they meet the standards.
notes.explanation: Every standard in 97.317(a) must be met, and the gain limit is 15 dB.
notes.source: 47 CFR Part 97 (rev. 1 Oct 2025), § 97.317(a)(2) Standards for certification of external RF power amplifiers
notes.evidence: Not be capable of amplifying the input RF power (driving signal) by more than 15 dB gain.

notes.front: Your employer asks you to use your station to order spare parts for the company from a supplier. May you?
notes.choices:
A) Yes, if the order is worth less than $25
B) Yes, if you are not paid for the call
C) No: it is a communication on behalf of your employer, in which you have a pecuniary interest
D) Yes, if the supplier is also a licensed amateur
notes.back: No: it is a communication on behalf of your employer, in which you have a pecuniary interest
notes.choicesExplained: A: Part 97 sets no money threshold. B: the ban covers communications on behalf of an employer, paid or not. D: the supplier’s licence does not change the purpose of the message.
notes.explanation: Part 97 names communications on behalf of an employer, subject only to its listed exceptions.
notes.evidence: Communications in which the station licensee or control operator has a pecuniary interest, including communications on behalf of an employer, with the following exceptions:

notes.front: Elements 2 and 3 versus Element 4: how many questions, and how many correct to pass?
notes.back: Elements 2 and 3: 35 questions, 26 to pass. Element 4: 50 questions, 37 to pass.
notes.explanation: Section 97.503 sets each written element’s size and pass mark.
notes.evidence: (b) Element 3: 35 questions concerning the privileges of a General Class operator license. The minimum passing score is 26 questions answered correctly. (c) Element 4: 50 questions concerning the privileges of an Amateur Extra Class operator license. The minimum passing score is 37 questions answered correctly.

notes.front: Which licence class must a VE hold to give a General exam, versus an Amateur Extra exam?
notes.back: General exam: Amateur Extra or Advanced. Amateur Extra exam: Amateur Extra only.
notes.explanation: A Technician exam may also be given by General class VEs.
notes.source: 47 CFR Part 97 (rev. 1 Oct 2025), § 97.509(b)(3) Administering VE requirements
notes.evidence: (i) Amateur Extra, Advanced or General Class in order to administer a Technician Class operator license examination; (ii) Amateur Extra or Advanced Class in order to administer a General Class operator license examination; (iii) Amateur Extra Class in order to administer an Amateur Extra Class operator license examination.

notes.front: Operating in the United States under reciprocal authority: where does a Canadian licensee put the location indicator, versus other foreign licensees?
notes.back: Canadian licensees: after the call sign. Other foreign licensees: before it.
notes.explanation: The indicator is the letter-numeral designating the station location.
notes.evidence: an indicator consisting of the appropriate letter-numeral designating the station location must be included before the call sign that was issued to the station by the country granting the license. For an amateur service license granted by the Government of Canada, however, the indicator must be included after the call sign.

notes.front: What may a VE accept from examinees, and what may they not?
notes.back: May accept: reimbursement of permitted out-of-pocket expenses. May not: any other money or consideration, or reimbursement beyond what is permitted.
notes.explanation: The ban covers fraudulent means as well as monetary or other consideration.
notes.source: 47 CFR Part 97 (rev. 1 Oct 2025), § 97.509(e) Administering VE requirements
notes.evidence: No VE may administer or certify any examination by fraudulent means or for monetary or other consideration including reimbursement in any amount in excess of that permitted.

notes.front: For which types of out-of-pocket expenses do the Part 97 rules state that VEs and VECs may be reimbursed?
notes.choices:
A) Preparing, processing, administering, and coordinating an examination for an amateur radio operator license
B) Teaching an amateur operator license examination preparation course
C) No expenses are authorized for reimbursement
D) Providing amateur operator license examination preparation training materials
notes.back: Preparing, processing, administering, and coordinating an examination for an amateur radio operator license
notes.choicesExplained: B and D: courses and training materials are not the examination expenses named in 97.527. C: reimbursement is authorised.
notes.explanation: Section 97.527 lets examinees reimburse VEs and VECs for out-of-pocket expenses in preparing, processing, administering or coordinating an examination.
notes.evidence:
A. Preparing, processing, administering, and coordinating an examination for an amateur radio operator
license

notes.front: Who is tasked by Part 97 with maintaining the pools of questions for all US amateur license examinations?
notes.choices:
A) The VEs
B) The FCC
C) The VECs
D) The ARRL
notes.back: The VECs
notes.choicesExplained: A: VEs prepare questions, but the pools are the VECs’ task. B: the rule gives the task to the VECs, not the FCC. D: the rule names no single organisation.
notes.explanation: Section 97.523 has all VECs cooperate in maintaining one question pool for each written element.
notes.evidence:
E1E02 (C) [97.523]
Who is tasked by Part 97 with maintaining the pools of questions for all US amateur license
examinations?
A. The VEs
B. The FCC
C. The VECs
D. The ARRL

notes.front: What is a Volunteer Examiner Coordinator?
notes.choices:
A) A person who has volunteered to administer amateur operator license examinations
B) An organization paid by the volunteer examiner team to publicize and schedule examinations
C) An organization that has entered into an agreement with the FCC to coordinate, prepare, and administer amateur operator license examinations
D) The person who has entered into an agreement with the FCC to be the VE session manager
notes.back: An organization that has entered into an agreement with the FCC to coordinate, prepare, and administer amateur operator license examinations
notes.choicesExplained: A and D: a VEC is an organisation, not a person. B: a VEC is not paid by the VE team; it holds an agreement with the FCC.
notes.explanation: Section 97.521 says no organisation may serve as a VEC without a written agreement with the FCC.
notes.evidence:
C. An organization that has entered into an agreement with the FCC to coordinate, prepare, and
administer amateur operator license examinations

notes.front: What is required to be accredited as a Volunteer Examiner?
notes.choices:
A) Each General, Advanced and Amateur Extra class operator is automatically accredited as a VE when the license is granted
B) The amateur operator applying must pass a VE examination administered by the FCC Enforcement Bureau
C) The prospective VE must obtain accreditation from the FCC
D) A VEC must confirm that the VE applicant meets FCC requirements to serve as an examiner
notes.back: A VEC must confirm that the VE applicant meets FCC requirements to serve as an examiner
notes.choicesExplained: A: accreditation is not automatic on licence grant. B: no FCC examination for VEs appears in these rules. C: accreditation comes from a VEC, not the FCC.
notes.explanation: Each administering VE must be accredited by the coordinating VEC (97.509(b)(1)), and 97.525 sets when a VEC may not accredit someone.
notes.evidence: D. A VEC must confirm that the VE applicant meets FCC requirements to serve as an examiner

notes.front: What must the VE team do with the application form if the examinee does not pass the exam?
notes.choices:
A) Maintain the application form with the VEC’s records
B) Return the application document to the examinee
C) Send the application form to the FCC and inform the FCC of the grade
D) Destroy the application form
notes.back: Return the application document to the examinee
notes.choicesExplained: A, C and D: the rule says to return it to the examinee, not to keep, forward or destroy it.
notes.explanation: Section 97.509(j) says the VEs must return the application document to the examinee and tell them the grade.
notes.evidence: B. Return the application document to the examinee

notes.front: Who is responsible for the proper conduct and necessary supervision during an amateur operator license examination session?
notes.choices:
A) The VEC coordinating the session
B) The designated monitoring VE
C) Each administering VE
D) Only the VE session manager
notes.back: Each administering VE
notes.choicesExplained: A: the VEC coordinates, but supervision rests with the administering VEs. B and D: the rule gives no single VE this duty; it falls on each administering VE.
notes.explanation: Section 97.509(c) makes the administering VEs responsible for the proper conduct and necessary supervision of each examination.
notes.evidence:
E1E06 (C) [97.509]
Who is responsible for the proper conduct and necessary supervision during an amateur operator
license examination session?
A. The VEC coordinating the session
B. The designated monitoring VE
C. Each administering VE
D. Only the VE session manager

notes.front: What should a VE do if a candidate fails to comply with the examiner’s instructions during an amateur operator license examination?
notes.choices:
A) Warn the candidate that continued failure to comply will result in termination of the examination
B) Immediately terminate the candidate’s examination
C) Allow the candidate to complete the examination, but invalidate the results
D) Immediately terminate everyone’s examination and close the session
notes.back: Immediately terminate the candidate’s examination
notes.choicesExplained: A: no warning step is provided. C: the exam is stopped, not completed. D: only the non-complying candidate’s exam is stopped.
notes.explanation: Section 97.509(c) says the administering VEs must immediately terminate the examination when the examinee fails to comply with their instructions.
notes.evidence:
E1E07 (B) [97.509, 97.511]
What should a VE do if a candidate fails to comply with the examiner’s instructions during an amateur
operator license examination?
A. Warn the candidate that continued failure to comply will result in termination of the examination
B. Immediately terminate the candidate’s examination
C. Allow the candidate to complete the examination, but invalidate the results

notes.front: To which of the following examinees may a VE not administer an examination?
notes.choices:
A) Employees of the VE
B) Friends of the VE
C) Relatives of the VE as listed in the FCC rules
D) All these choices are correct
notes.back: Relatives of the VE as listed in the FCC rules
notes.choicesExplained: A and B: employees and friends are not on the list. D: so not all are correct.
notes.explanation: Section 97.509(d) lists the relatives, from spouse to in-laws, whom a VE may not examine.
notes.evidence: C. Relatives of the VE as listed in the FCC rules

notes.front: What may be the penalty for a VE who fraudulently administers or certifies an examination?
notes.choices:
A) Revocation of the VE’s amateur station license grant and the suspension of the VE’s amateur operator license grant
B) A fine of up to $1,000 per occurrence
C) A sentence of up to one year in prison
D) All these choices are correct
notes.back: Revocation of the VE’s amateur station license grant and the suspension of the VE’s amateur operator license grant
notes.choicesExplained: B and C: 97.509(e) names licence penalties, not a fine or prison. D: so not all are correct.
notes.explanation: Section 97.509(e) says fraud may bring revocation of the VE’s station licence grant and suspension of the operator licence grant.
notes.evidence:
A. Revocation of the VE’s amateur station license grant and the suspension of the VE’s amateur operator
license grant

notes.front: What must the administering VEs do after the administration of a successful examination for an amateur operator license?
notes.choices:
A) They must collect and send the documents directly to the FCC
B) They must collect and submit the documents to the coordinating VEC for grading
C) They must submit the application document to the coordinating VEC according to the coordinating VEC instructions
D) They must return the documents to the applicant for submission to the FCC according to the FCC instructions
notes.back: They must submit the application document to the coordinating VEC according to the coordinating VEC instructions
notes.choicesExplained: A, B and D: the document goes to the coordinating VEC, not elsewhere.
notes.explanation: Section 97.509(m) requires the application document to go to the coordinating VEC, following that VEC’s instructions.
notes.evidence:
C. They must submit the application document to the coordinating VEC according to the coordinating
VEC instructions

notes.front: What must the VE team do if an examinee scores a passing grade on all examination elements needed for an upgrade or new license?
notes.choices:
A) Photocopy all examination documents and forward them to the FCC for processing
B) Three VEs must certify that the examinee is qualified for the license grant and that they have complied with the administering VE requirements
C) Issue the examinee the new or upgrade license
D) All these choices are correct
notes.back: Three VEs must certify that the examinee is qualified for the license grant and that they have complied with the administering VE requirements
notes.choicesExplained: A, C and D: the rule asks for certification by three VEs, not these other steps.
notes.explanation: Section 97.509(i) requires 3 VEs to certify both the examinee's qualification and their own compliance; the first errata, of 31 January 2024, corrected the pool's citation from (m) to (i).
notes.evidence:
B. Three VEs must certify that the examinee is qualified for the license grant and that they have
complied with the administering VE requirements

notes.front: On what frequencies are spread spectrum transmissions permitted?
notes.choices:
A) Only on amateur frequencies above 50 MHz
B) Only on amateur frequencies above 222 MHz
C) Only on amateur frequencies above 420 MHz
D) Only on amateur frequencies above 144 MHz
notes.back: Only on amateur frequencies above 222 MHz
notes.choicesExplained: A and D: the 6 m and 2 m entries do not list SS. C: SS is already authorised at 222–225 MHz, below 420 MHz.
notes.explanation: In the 97.305(c) table, SS first appears in the 222–225 MHz segment; the pool keys “above 222 MHz”.
notes.evidence: B. Only on amateur frequencies above 222 MHz

notes.front: What privileges are authorized in the US to persons holding an amateur service license granted by the government of Canada?
notes.choices:
A) None, they must obtain a US license
B) Full privileges of the General class license on the 80-, 40-, 20-, 15-, and 10-meter bands
C) The operating terms and conditions of the Canadian amateur service license, not to exceed US Amateur Extra class license privileges
D) Full privileges, up to and including those of the Amateur Extra class license, on the 80-, 40-, 20-, 15-, and 10-meter bands
notes.back: The operating terms and conditions of the Canadian amateur service license, not to exceed US Amateur Extra class license privileges
notes.choicesExplained: A: Canadian licensees do not need a US licence to operate. B and D: privileges follow the Canadian licence, not a fixed list of bands.
notes.explanation: Section 97.107(a) grants a Canadian licensee the terms of the Canadian licence and the Part 97 rules, not exceeding Amateur Extra Class privileges.
notes.evidence:
C. The operating terms and conditions of the Canadian amateur service license, not to exceed US
Amateur Extra class license privileges

notes.front: Under what circumstances may a dealer sell an external RF power amplifier capable of operation below 144 MHz if it has not been granted FCC certification?
notes.choices:
A) Gain is less than 23 dB when driven by power of 10 watts or less
B) The equipment dealer assembled it from a kit
C) It was manufactured and certificated in a country which has a reciprocal certification agreement with the FCC
D) The amplifier is constructed or modified by an amateur radio operator for use at an amateur station
notes.back: The amplifier is constructed or modified by an amateur radio operator for use at an amateur station
notes.choicesExplained: A: 97.315 has no gain exception. B: a dealer is not an amateur building for amateur use. C: 97.315 mentions no reciprocal certification agreement.
notes.explanation: Section 97.315(b)(1) exempts an amplifier built or modified by an amateur operator for use at an amateur station; that paragraph survived the February 2026 clean-up.
notes.evidence: D. The amplifier is constructed or modified by an amateur radio operator for use at an amateur station

notes.front: Which of the following geographic descriptions approximately describes "Line A"?
notes.choices:
A) A line roughly parallel to and south of the border between the US and Canada
B) A line roughly parallel to and west of the US Atlantic coastline
C) A line roughly parallel to and north of the border between the US and Mexico
D) A line roughly parallel to and east of the US Pacific coastline
notes.back: A line roughly parallel to and south of the border between the US and Canada
notes.choicesExplained: B, C and D: Line A runs along the northern border, not along the Atlantic or Pacific coast or the Mexican border.
notes.explanation: Part 97 traces Line A from Aberdeen, Washington, across to Searsport, Maine, just south of the border with Canada.
notes.evidence: A. A line roughly parallel to and south of the border between the US and Canada

notes.front: Amateur stations may not transmit in which of the following frequency segments if they are located in the contiguous 48 states and north of Line A?
notes.choices:
A) 440 MHz - 450 MHz
B) 53 MHz - 54 MHz
C) 222 MHz - 223 MHz
D) 420 MHz - 430 MHz
notes.back: 420 MHz - 430 MHz
notes.choicesExplained: A, B and C: the Line A ban applies to 420–430 MHz only.
notes.explanation: Section 97.303(m)(1) says no amateur station shall transmit from north of Line A in the 420–430 MHz segment.
notes.evidence:

notes.front: Under what circumstances might the FCC issue a Special Temporary Authority (STA) to an amateur station?
notes.choices:
A) To provide for experimental amateur communications
B) To allow use of a special event call sign
C) To allow a VE group with less than three VEs to administer examinations in a remote, sparsely populated area
D) To allow a licensee who has passed an upgrade exam to operate with upgraded privileges while waiting for posting on the FCC database
notes.back: To provide for experimental amateur communications
notes.choicesExplained: B: special event call signs have their own procedure in 97.119(d). C: 97.509(a) requires a team of at least 3 VEs. D: no STA is needed, since 97.9(b) lets a successful examinee with a CSCE use the higher privileges while the application is pending.
notes.explanation: The pool keys experimental amateur communications; it cites FCC rule 1.931, which this deck has not checked.
notes.evidence: A. To provide for experimental amateur communications

notes.front: When may an amateur station send a message to a business?
notes.choices:
A) When the pecuniary interest of the amateur or his or her employer is less than $25
B) When the pecuniary interest of the amateur or his or her employer is less than $50
C) At no time
D) When neither the amateur nor their employer has a pecuniary interest in the communications
notes.back: When neither the amateur nor their employer has a pecuniary interest in the communications
notes.choicesExplained: A and B: Part 97 sets no money threshold. C: a message to a business is allowed when no one has a pecuniary interest in it.
notes.explanation: Section 97.113(a)(3) bars communications in which the licensee or control operator has a pecuniary interest, including those on behalf of an employer.
notes.evidence: D. When neither the amateur nor their employer has a pecuniary interest in the communications

notes.front: Which of the following types of amateur station communications are prohibited?
notes.choices:
A) Communications transmitted for hire or material compensation, except as otherwise provided in the rules
B) Communications that have political content, except as allowed by the Fairness Doctrine
C) Communications that have religious content
D) Communications in a language other than English
notes.back: Communications transmitted for hire or material compensation, except as otherwise provided in the rules
notes.choicesExplained: B, C and D: 97.113 does not bar political or religious content or languages other than English.
notes.explanation: Part 97 bars communications for hire or material compensation in 97.113(a)(2); the pool’s citation of 97.113(c) is out of date, as that paragraph covers retransmission.
notes.evidence:
A. Communications transmitted for hire or material compensation, except as otherwise provided in the
rules

notes.front: Which of the following cannot be transmitted over an amateur radio mesh network?
notes.choices:
A) Third party traffic
B) Email
C) Messages encoded to obscure their meaning
D) All these choices are correct
notes.back: Messages encoded to obscure their meaning
notes.choicesExplained: A and B: third-party traffic and email are not banned by this rule. D: so not all are correct.
notes.explanation: Section 97.113(a)(4) prohibits messages encoded for the purpose of obscuring their meaning, and a mesh network is no exception.
notes.evidence: C. Messages encoded to obscure their meaning

notes.front: Who may be the control operator of an auxiliary station?
notes.choices:
A) Any licensed amateur operator
B) Only Technician, General, Advanced, or Amateur Extra class operators
C) Only General, Advanced, or Amateur Extra class operators
D) Only Amateur Extra class operators
notes.back: Only Technician, General, Advanced, or Amateur Extra class operators
notes.choicesExplained: A: the rule names these four classes, not any licensee. C and D: Technicians are included.
notes.explanation: Section 97.201(a) lets a Technician, General, Advanced or Amateur Extra Class licensee be an auxiliary station’s control operator.
notes.evidence: B. Only Technician, General, Advanced, or Amateur Extra class operators

notes.front: Which of the following best describes one of the standards that must be met by an external RF power amplifier if it is to qualify for a grant of FCC certification?
notes.choices:
A) It must produce full legal output when driven by not more than 5 watts of mean RF input power
B) It must have received an Underwriters Laboratory certification for electrical safety as well as having met IEEE standard 14.101(B)
C) It must exhibit a gain of less than 23 dB when driven by 10 watts or less
D) It must satisfy the FCC’s spurious emission standards when operated at the lesser of 1500 watts or its full output power
notes.back: It must satisfy the FCC’s spurious emission standards when operated at the lesser of 1500 watts or its full output power
notes.choicesExplained: A and C: 97.317 limits gain to 15 dB; it neither requires full output from 5 W nor allows 23 dB. B: the rule names no laboratory or standards-body certification.
notes.explanation: Section 97.317(a)(1) requires the spurious emission standards to be met at the lesser of 1.5 kW PEP or full output, and in standby or off.
notes.evidence:
D. It must satisfy the FCC’s spurious emission standards when operated at the lesser of 1500 watts or its
full output power
